input_signals.name: Cash-Backed Gross Profitability
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross profitability should be most valuable when supported by a strong cash reserve that reduces financing distress risk.
input_signals.reasoning: Gross profit quality can be fragile if the firm lacks liquidity, while cash alone may simply reflect precautionary hoarding or weak investment opportunities. The product structure favors firms that jointly have durable operating economics and balance-sheet liquidity, rather than merely high quality or merely low distress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( che, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Revenue Trend Liquidity Confirmation
input_signals.hypothesis: Improving revenue productivity should predict stronger returns when supported by positive working-capital capacity.
input_signals.reasoning: Revenue growth or asset turnover improvement can be low quality if it consumes liquidity or reflects aggressive credit extension. Requiring a working-capital cushion makes the quality trend more likely to represent self-financing operating improvement rather than distress-inducing expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( trend( ratio( revt, at ), 5 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( wcap, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Gross Profit Liquidity Repair
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(che, at), 1), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(lt, at), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Improving gross profitability should predict higher returns when accompanied by balance-sheet repair through rising cash intensity and falling liability intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids using taxes or pre-tax income as a second profitability proxy. The distress leg is explicitly about liquidity rebuilding and deleveraging, so the signal tests whether operating-quality improvement is more valuable when financial distress pressure is actively easing.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( trend( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), at ), 5 ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ), neg( delta( ratio( lt, at ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self-Financed Sales Improvement
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(revt, at), 5)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(wcap, at), 1)), RATIO(che, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Improving revenue productivity should predict higher returns when growth is not being funded by rising working-capital needs and the firm retains a cash cushion.
input_signals.reasoning: This keeps the successful revenue-productivity mechanism but aligns the working-capital leg with accrual evidence: lower working-capital buildup is favorable. The cash component helps separate efficient self-financed expansion from distressed liquidation of working capital.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( trend( ratio( revt, at ), 5 ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( neg( delta( ratio( wcap, at ), 1 ) ), ratio( che, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash Conversion Solvency Quality
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, revt), 3)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, at), NEG(RATIO(lt, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that convert sales into operating cash flow should earn higher returns when that cash-conversion quality is paired with a solvent, liquid balance sheet.
input_signals.reasoning: Operating cash flow scaled by revenue captures cash-conversion quality rather than simple profitability. Combining it with cash reserves and low liabilities tests whether cash-generation quality is most predictive when distress risk is already being contained.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( che, at ), neg( ratio( lt, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stable Cash Conversion Short-Debt Shield
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, revt), 5))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, at), NEG(RATIO(dlc, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Stable cash conversion should predict higher returns when near-term debt pressure is limited and cash liquidity is strong.
input_signals.reasoning: Prior margin-volatility ideas were weak, so this shifts the stability concept from accounting margins to operating cash conversion. Stability in cash generation is most useful to equity holders when short-maturity debt is not forcing refinancing at unfavorable terms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( oancf, revt ), 5 ) ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( che, at ), neg( ratio( dlc, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Positive Accounting Distress
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, revt), 3)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(pi, at)), RATIO(che, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong cash conversion should earn higher returns when accounting distress is present but liquidity provides time for recovery.
input_signals.reasoning: Pre-tax losses alone are distress signals, but they are less damning when sales still convert into operating cash and the firm holds cash. The interaction targets cash-quality recoveries among accounting-distressed firms rather than a generic high-profitability or low-distress screen.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oancf, revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( neg( ratio( pi, at ) ), ratio( che, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Supplier-Financed Gross Margin Quality
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 3)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(wcap, at)), RATIO(che, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High gross margins should be especially valuable when negative working capital is paired with cash reserves, indicating efficient supplier financing rather than liquidity distress.
input_signals.reasoning: Low or negative working capital can signal distress, but for firms with strong unit economics and cash reserves it may instead reflect favorable operating terms. This signal tests whether quality helps distinguish efficient working-capital models from genuinely distressed balance sheets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( neg( ratio( wcap, at ) ), ratio( che, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Fixable Leakage Cash Franchise
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 3), MA(RATIO(oancf, revt), 3))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), pi), at), RATIO(che, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong gross margins and cash conversion should outperform when below-gross leakage depresses pre-tax income but cash reserves preserve recovery optionality.
input_signals.reasoning: This treats the gap between gross profit and pre-tax income as a potentially fixable distress burden rather than automatically bad profitability. The quality leg requires both unit economics and cash conversion, while the cash cushion reduces the risk that below-line pressure forces distress before recovery.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( sumrank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 3 ), ma( ratio( oancf, revt ), 3 ) ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), pi ), at ), ratio( che, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin Improvement Current-Asset Quality
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 3)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, act), NEG(RATIO(lct, act)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Improving gross margins should predict stronger returns when current assets are cash-heavy and not overwhelmed by current liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the duplicated cash-conversion level and instead tests whether margin improvement is more credible when liquidity quality is high. Scaling cash and current liabilities by current assets focuses on near-term balance-sheet composition rather than a cosmetic che/at versus che/act rescaling of the prior cash-conversion signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( trend( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( che, act ), neg( ratio( lct, act ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Supplier-Financed Sales Productivity
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(revt, at), 3)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(wcap, at)), RATIO(che, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High sales productivity should predict stronger returns when negative working capital is supported by cash reserves, indicating efficient supplier financing rather than distress.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the low-volatility template and the repeated cash-minus-short-debt leg. The interaction asks whether quality in asset productivity helps distinguish productive negative-working-capital business models from firms whose low working capital reflects liquidity stress.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( revt, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( neg( ratio( wcap, at ) ), ratio( che, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating Float Cash Franchise
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 3), MA(RATIO(oancf, revt), 3))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), at), RATIO(che, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong margins and cash conversion should outperform when current liabilities are primarily operating float rather than short debt and cash reserves are high.
input_signals.reasoning: Current liabilities are not always distress; for high-quality firms, non-debt current liabilities can reflect supplier financing or favorable operating terms. The signal separates productive operating float from refinancing risk by excluding debt due within one year from the float leg and requiring cash-backed operating quality.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( sumrank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 3 ), ma( ratio( oancf, revt ), 3 ) ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), at ), ratio( che, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Current-Asset Turnover Refinancing Shield
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(revt, act), 3)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(che, at), NEG(RATIO(dlc, lct)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with productive current assets should outperform when cash reserves are strong and current liabilities are not dominated by debt due within one year.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the margin-trough/current-asset leg swap with a distinct operating-cycle mechanism. High current-asset turnover indicates efficient conversion of short-term assets into sales, while the distress leg separates ordinary operating liabilities from refinancing-sensitive current debt.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( revt, act ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( che, at ), neg( ratio( dlc, lct ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working-Capital Float Regime Quality
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 3), MA(RATIO(oancf, revt), 3))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(wcap, at), 5)), RATIO(che, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with strong margins and cash conversion should outperform when working capital is low relative to their own history but cash reserves remain high.
input_signals.reasoning: Low working capital is ambiguous: it can indicate distress or an efficient float model. Conditioning on strong gross margins, cash conversion, and cash holdings treats a low within-firm working-capital regime as operational efficiency rather than liquidity exhaustion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( sumrank( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 3 ), ma( ratio( oancf, revt ), 3 ) ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( neg( ts_rank( ratio( wcap, at ), 5 ) ), ratio( che, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating Claims Sales Coverage Trap
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(lct, dlc), revt)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 3)), NEG(RATIO(che, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating current claims relative to sales should be bearish when gross margins are weak and cash reserves are low.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids reusing the current-asset-turnover leg and reframes non-debt current liabilities as a claims burden rather than productive float. Operating liabilities are most likely to reflect supplier pressure when sales coverage is thin, margins are weak, and cash liquidity is scarce.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), revt ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( neg( ma( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 3 ) ), neg( ratio( che, at ) ) ) ) )
